reviewed_findings.why: Actual /bin/busybox is the locally rebuilt fixed payload 68dba7ae251db2ecca77e6ef405bf781111dc41f87c93c30205745fdbe2c697e. The HTTP send path now checks the actual target.path and target.host for raw non-NUL C0, SP and DEL immediately before opening the socket, including relative/absolute redirect reuse and proxy absolute-form. Exact bytes/config/source/patch are bound to the combined runtime. Real regressions retain normal/percent-encoded requests, reject raw controls/spaces before injection traffic, and reproduce the original defects in the target rootfs. Original APK version is preserved; this is a custom verified code backport, not an official Alpine revision bump. A raw NUL cannot be embedded in an OS argv/C-string component; the regression preserves percent-encoded %00 as literal encoded bytes rather than claiming an executable raw-NUL test.
reviewed_findings.primary_fixed_or_affected_scope: CNA concerns wget raw C0/CR/LF/SP in HTTP request-target; no mature official fixed-version entry is assumed. Exact local boundary backport fixes wget only; ssl_client is independently scoped as TLS transport.

reviewed_findings.why: Current runtime /bin/sh is a symlink to /bin/busybox, whose actual payload hash is 68dba7ae251db2ecca77e6ef405bf781111dc41f87c93c30205745fdbe2c697e. busybox-binsh owns this symlink and depends on busybox=1.37.0-r31; there is no second independent wget ELF under this package. The sole shared wget implementation is the exact fixed binary covered by the source patch and 50/53 real regressions. This preserves the scanner package match without pretending that three independent vulnerability implementations were repaired.

reviewed_findings.why: Current /usr/bin/ssl_client is the separate unchanged TLS helper ELF 8b23a9dbfea3da8c6da65b93c0fc6d979a82245c17c40d8fbf94d531263b98b4. The exact official Alpine source, verified against the APKBUILD SHA512, accepts an existing fd/SNI, negotiates TLS and copies stdin/TLS/stdout using SSL_read/SSL_write. It does not parse URLs or construct HTTP request-target/request-line/header bytes; the affected implementation is BusyBox networking/wget.c. Its broad APK source-origin match therefore does not establish the affected HTTP-construction code in this helper. For its actual wget caller the HTTP fields are validated by the sole fixed BusyBox payload before connection. This is not a claim that arbitrary caller-provided plaintext is sanitized by a protocol-agnostic TLS transport.
